stairs_cop.result: cause found: bug, not the plate frame and not the heading fallback
stairs_cop.detail: The foot-frame pressure point is computed from COPX and COPZ with the height forced to 0. In stairs the source plate COPY_Vertical is 0.35 to 0.83 m (AB12 stairs_1_10: L 0.51, R 0.35; AB02 stairs_1_9: L 0.66, R 0.50; AB08 stairs_1_1: L 0.83, R 0.67) and the heel marker height during load follows it (0.06 to 0.1 m above it). So the vertical foot-frame coordinate is -0.4 to -0.9 m (median in my sample: -0.57 to -0.89) and the forward coordinate is distorted by the tilt of the foot. Re-running my own computation with COPY_Vertical gives a median vertical -0.065 to -0.096 m and outside-by-5-cm share 0 to 3% (AB12 stairs_1_10 0.00, AB05 stairs_1_7 0.00 to 0.01, AB08 stairs_1_1 0.01, AB02 stairs_1_9 0.02 to 0.03), against 25 to 100% as converted. Level walking has COPY = 0, which is why the pilots passed. Heading fallback is not involved: the pressure point does not use heading.
stairs_cop.likely_also_affected: Published ankle moment ratio 0.35 on stairs is expected to rise once the vertical offset is fixed (the moment arm used the wrong height); not recomputed.
stairs_cop.curb_and_other_tasks: AB03 curb_up_1 still has median vertical -0.247 m and 10 to 12% outside after using COPY_Vertical: its COPY is about 0.009 m while the heel marker rises to 0.22 to 0.43 m during load. Not explained (may be samples on the curb, not on the plate). The worker summary also lists curb_down 11%, curb_up 13%, cutting 18% median outside share. Not checked here.

The stairs foot-frame pressure point is wrong because of a bug: the code puts the plate pressure point at height 0, but on the stairs the plate surface is 0.35 to 0.83 m above the lab floor and the source gives that height in the COPY_Vertical column.
